description: Benchmark for Python 3.13 docs subset. Written and split dev/test BEFORE any retrieval run. gold[].pages is filled by `python -m src.run validate`, which locates each evidence quote in the normalized page units (no retrieval involved).
split_rule: Test questions were chosen from sections that no dev question targets (tut-errors 8.7 clean-up, tut-modules 6.1.2 search path, lib-csv reader(), lib-functools lru_cache, lib-json dumps keys note, tut-venv activation). Same documents appear in both splits -> leakage risk at document level, noted in report.
filter_rule: filter = doc_type the user states up front (e.g. 'I am reading the tutorial' / 'in the library reference'); provided before retrieval, never derived from the gold source. Strategy C applies it only when present.
selection_criterion: Decided before test: choose by dev Evidence Hit@3, tie-break dev Hit@1, then fewer chunks / less embed time.

questions.question: When does the else clause of a for loop run?
questions.expected_answer: After the loop finishes its final iteration, i.e. only if no break occurred.

gold.evidence_quote: In a "for" loop, the "else" clause is executed after the loop finishes its final iteration, that is, if no break occurred.

questions.question: Why does a function with a list as default argument keep accumulating values between calls?
questions.expected_answer: Default values are evaluated only once (at definition), so a mutable default like a list is shared across calls.

gold.evidence_quote: The default value is evaluated only once. This makes a difference when the default is a mutable object such as a list, dictionary, or instances of most classes.

questions.question: How do I mark function parameters as positional-only?
questions.expected_answer: Place them before a / (forward slash) in the parameter list.

gold.evidence_quote: Positional-only parameters are placed before a "/" (forward-slash).

questions.question: What should I use instead of a plain list to get an efficient first-in first-out queue?
questions.expected_answer: collections.deque, designed for fast appends and pops from both ends.

gold.evidence_quote: To implement a queue, use "collections.deque" which was designed to have fast appends and pops from both ends.

questions.question: Why doesn't {} give me an empty set?
questions.expected_answer: {} creates an empty dictionary; use set() for an empty set.

gold.evidence_quote: to create an empty set you have to use "set()", not "{}"; the latter creates an empty dictionary

questions.question: Can a tuple be used as a dictionary key?
questions.expected_answer: Yes, if it contains only strings, numbers or tuples; not if it contains any mutable object.

gold.evidence_quote: Tuples can be used as keys if they contain only strings, numbers, or tuples; if a tuple contains any mutable object either directly or indirectly, it cannot be used as a key.

questions.question: How can I suppress automatic exception chaining when I re-raise a different exception?
questions.expected_answer: Use `raise NewError from None`.

gold.evidence_quote: It also allows disabling automatic exception chaining using the "from None" idiom:

questions.question: How do I attach extra information to an exception after it was caught?
questions.expected_answer: Call the exception's add_note(note) method; notes are shown in the traceback.

gold.evidence_quote: exceptions have a method "add_note(note)" that accepts a string and adds it to the exception's notes list.

questions.question: How can I handle only some exception types contained in an ExceptionGroup?
questions.expected_answer: Use except* clauses, which extract matching exceptions from the group.

gold.evidence_quote: By using "except*" instead of "except", we can selectively handle only the exceptions in the group that match a certain type.

questions.question: Where does Python cache the compiled versions of modules?
questions.expected_answer: In the __pycache__ directory as module.<version>.pyc.

gold.evidence_quote: Python caches the compiled version of each module in the "__pycache__" directory under the name "module.*version*.pyc"

questions.question: What decides which submodules get imported by `from package import *`?
questions.expected_answer: The __all__ list defined in the package's __init__.py.

gold.evidence_quote: if a package's "__init__.py" code defines a list named "__all__", it is taken to be the list of module names that should be imported when "from package import *" is encountered.

questions.question: How can one Python file work both as a runnable script and as an importable module?
questions.expected_answer: Put the script code under `if __name__ == "__main__":` so it only runs when executed as the main file.

gold.evidence_quote: you can make the file usable as a script as well as an importable module, because the code that parses the command line only runs if the module is executed as the "main" file

questions.question: Why is it recommended to open files with the with keyword?
questions.expected_answer: The file is properly closed after the block, even if an exception is raised.

gold.evidence_quote: The advantage is that the file is properly closed after its suite finishes, even if an exception is raised at some point.

questions.question: I'm following the tutorial: how do I save a Python list to a text file as JSON?
questions.expected_answer: Use json.dump(x, f) with f a text file opened for writing.

gold.evidence_quote: Another variant of the "dumps()" function, called "dump()", simply serializes the object to a *text file*.

questions.question: In the tutorial, what command creates a new virtual environment?
questions.expected_answer: Run the venv module as a script with a directory: python -m venv tutorial-env.

gold.evidence_quote: To create a virtual environment, decide upon a directory where you want to place it, and run the "venv" module as a script with the directory path:

questions.question: Library reference: which venv option gives the environment access to the system site-packages?
questions.expected_answer: --system-site-packages

gold.evidence_quote: Give the virtual environment access to the system site-packages directory.

questions.question: How can I validate and pretty-print JSON from the command line?
questions.expected_answer: Use `python -m json.tool`.

gold.evidence_quote: The "json.tool" module provides a simple command line interface to validate and pretty-print JSON objects.
Using "json.tool" from the shell to validate and pretty-print:

questions.question: What happens when json serializes float('nan') with allow_nan set to False?
questions.expected_answer: It raises ValueError (strict JSON compliance).

gold.evidence_quote: will result in a "ValueError", in strict compliance with the JSON specification.
Otherwise, it will be a "ValueError" to encode such floats.

questions.question: How do I compute a property value once and keep it cached for the lifetime of the instance?
questions.expected_answer: Decorate the method with @functools.cached_property.

gold.evidence_quote: Transform a method of a class into a property whose value is computed once and then cached as a normal attribute for the life of the instance.

questions.question: On which argument does @singledispatch dispatch?
questions.expected_answer: On the type of the first argument.

gold.evidence_quote: note that the dispatch happens on the type of the first argument
the generic function dispatches on the type of the first argument

questions.question: If I don't pass fieldnames to csv.DictReader, where do the dictionary keys come from?
questions.expected_answer: From the first row of the file, which is then omitted from the results.

gold.evidence_quote: If *fieldnames* is omitted, the values in the first row of file *f* will be used as the fieldnames and will be omitted from the results.

questions.question: According to the library reference, should a virtual environment be committed to Git?
questions.expected_answer: No, it is not checked into source control systems such as Git.

gold.evidence_quote: Not checked into source control systems such as Git.

questions.question: If both the try block and the finally block contain a return statement, which value is returned?
questions.expected_answer: The value from the finally clause's return statement.

gold.evidence_quote: If a "finally" clause includes a "return" statement, the returned value will be the one from the "finally" clause's "return" statement, not the value from the "try" clause's "return" statement.

questions.question: Which locations is sys.path initialized from?
questions.expected_answer: The script's directory (or current directory), PYTHONPATH, and the installation-dependent default (site-packages).

gold.evidence_quote: "sys.path" is initialized from these locations: * The directory containing the input script (or the current directory when no file is specified). * "PYTHONPATH" (a list of directory names, with the same syntax as the shell variable "PATH"). * The installation-dependent default

questions.question: How should a file be opened before passing it to csv.reader?
questions.expected_answer: With newline=''.

gold.evidence_quote: If *csvfile* is a file object, it should be opened with "newline=''".

questions.question: What happens to lru_cache when maxsize is None?
questions.expected_answer: The LRU feature is disabled and the cache can grow without bound.

gold.evidence_quote: If *maxsize* is set to "None", the LRU feature is disabled and the cache can grow without bound.

questions.question: In the library reference: why may a dictionary not equal the original after converting it to JSON and back?
questions.expected_answer: JSON keys are always str, so non-string keys are converted to strings.

gold.evidence_quote: Keys in key/value pairs of JSON are always of the type "str". When a dictionary is converted into JSON, all the keys of the dictionary are converted to strings.

questions.question: Following the tutorial, how do I activate a virtual environment on Windows?
questions.expected_answer: Run tutorial-env\Scripts\activate.

gold.evidence_quote: On Windows, run: tutorial-env\Scripts\activate
